questions.text: This section is taken from which structure?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Sagittal section of the lip showing 3 distinct zones: the outer thin skin surface with hair follicles and sebaceous glands, the central core of skeletal muscle (orbicularis oris), and the inner mucosal surface lined by stratified squamous non-keratinized epithelium with submucosal labial glands.
questions.keyConcept: Lip histology: Thin skin, orbicularis oris muscle core, and oral mucosa.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Structure 1 represents the external cutaneous (skin) surface, covered by keratinized stratified squamous epithelium with hair follicles, sebaceous glands, and sweat glands.
questions.keyConcept: Cutaneous surface of lip.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Structure 2 shows hair follicles embedded in the dermis with associated sebaceous glands on the cutaneous surface.
questions.keyConcept: Skin appendages of the lip.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Structure 3 is the central muscle core formed by striated skeletal muscle fibers of the orbicularis oris muscle cut in cross and longitudinal sections.
questions.keyConcept: Orbicularis oris skeletal muscle core.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Structure 4 is the vermilion zone (red margin of the lip), the transition zone covered by modified translucent stratified squamous epithelium with tall, highly vascular dermal papillae close to the surface.
questions.keyConcept: Vermilion border (red margin): Translucent epithelium with rich capillary loops.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Submucosal mixed/mucous labial salivary glands embedded in connective tissue.
questions.keyConcept: Labial salivary glands.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The inner oral aspect is lined by moist, thick, non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium.
questions.keyConcept: Oral mucous membrane of lip.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Group of mixed, predominantly mucous tubuloacinar labial glands situated in the submucosa.
questions.keyConcept: Key identification criterion: Labial glands (Labial glands) — high-yield diagnostic spotter feature.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Striated skeletal muscle bundles of the orbicularis oris constituting the muscular framework of the lip.
questions.keyConcept: Key identification criterion: Orbicularis oris (Orbicularis oris muscle) — high-yield diagnostic spotter feature.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Submucosal labial salivary glands.
questions.keyConcept: Key identification criterion: Labial glands (Labial glands) — high-yield diagnostic spotter feature.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Internal oral mucosa lined by stratified squamous non-keratinized epithelium.
questions.keyConcept: Mucosa of the lip.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Vermilion border displaying high dermal vascular papillae.
questions.keyConcept: Red margin of lip.

questions.text: This section is taken from which structure?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Mass of interlacing skeletal muscle bundles covered by mucous membrane exhibiting characteristic dorsal lingual papillae.
questions.keyConcept: Tongue histology: Interlacing skeletal muscle with specialized dorsal papillae.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Numerous conical, pointed papillae covered by keratinized stratified squamous epithelium, lacking taste buds.
questions.keyConcept: Filiform papillae: Most numerous, conical, keratinized, purely mechanical (no taste buds).

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Bundles of skeletal muscle fibers arranged in three planes (longitudinal, transverse, and vertical).
questions.keyConcept: Lingual skeletal muscle.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Dense irregular collagenous connective tissue supporting the lingual epithelium.
questions.keyConcept: Lamina propria of tongue.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Serous and mucous lingual salivary glands embedded among the muscle bundles.
questions.keyConcept: Lingual salivary glands.

questions.text: Which type of lingual papilla is shown?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large, dome-shaped papilla surrounded by a deep circular furrow (moat) containing numerous lateral taste buds and receiving ducts of von Ebner serous glands.
questions.keyConcept: Circumvallate papilla: Large, sunken in moat, lateral taste buds, von Ebner serous glands at base.

questions.text: What do the arrows at the bottom point to?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Purely serous von Ebner glands located in the lamina propria whose watery secretion washes the circular moat around circumvallate papillae.
questions.keyConcept: Von Ebner glands: Purely serous glands flushing circumvallate grooves.

questions.text: Which type of lingual papilla is shown?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Slender, conical, keratinized spires.
questions.keyConcept: Filiform papillae.

questions.text: Which type of lingual papilla is shown?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Mushroom-shaped papilla with a narrow neck and expanded dome-shaped head covered by non-keratinized epithelium with taste buds on its dorsal surface.
questions.keyConcept: Fungiform papillae: Mushroom-shaped with apical taste buds.

questions.text: Which type of lingual papilla is shown?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Broad papilla surrounded by deep trench lined by taste buds.
questions.keyConcept: Circumvallate papillae.

questions.text: What is the structure outlined by the dashed line?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Pale-staining, barrel-shaped intraepithelial sensory organ opening via an apical taste pore.
questions.keyConcept: Taste bud: Barrel-shaped sensory organ containing gustatory, supporting, and basal cells.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Small apical opening through which sensory microvilli contact dissolved tastants.
questions.keyConcept: Key identification criterion: Taste pore (Taste pore) — high-yield diagnostic spotter feature.

questions.text: What do the arrows labeled 2 point to?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Small rounded regenerative stem cells located at the base of the taste bud.
questions.keyConcept: Basal cells: Regenerative stem cell population of taste bud.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Underlying connective tissue stroma.
questions.keyConcept: Key identification criterion: Lamina propria (Lamina propria) — high-yield diagnostic spotter feature.

questions.text: What is shown in this image?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Rounded acini with narrow lumina, basophilic basal cytoplasm (rich in RER), spherical basal nuclei, and apical eosinophilic zymogen granules.
questions.keyConcept: Serous acini: Spherical, basophilic base, round central/basal nucleus, narrow lumen.

questions.text: What is shown in this image?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Tubular/rounded acini with wide lumina, pale foamy cytoplasm filled with mucigen droplets, and flattened nuclei compressed against the basement membrane.
questions.keyConcept: Mucous acini: Wide lumen, pale vacuolated cytoplasm, flattened peripheral basal nuclei.

questions.text: What is the structure enclosed by the circle?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Mucous acinus capped by a crescent-shaped hood of serous cells (serous demilune of Giannuzzi).
questions.keyConcept: Mixed acinus with serous demilune.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Crescentic cap of serous cells surmounting a mucous tubule.
questions.keyConcept: Serous demilune of Giannuzzi.

questions.text: What do the lines at the center of the circle point to?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Central secretory lumen of the acinus.
questions.keyConcept: Key identification criterion: Acinar lumen (Lumen) — high-yield diagnostic spotter feature.

questions.text: What type of acini is shown?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Conspicuous mixed acinar architecture with serous crescents.
questions.keyConcept: Mixed salivary gland.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Crescent of Giannuzzi.
questions.keyConcept: Key identification criterion: Serous demilune (Serous demilune) — high-yield diagnostic spotter feature.

questions.text: What do the lines at the bottom point to?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Pale pyramidal cells with flattened basal nuclei.
questions.keyConcept: Key identification criterion: Mucous cells (Mucus-secreting cells) — high-yield diagnostic spotter feature.

questions.text: This section is taken from which gland?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Salivary gland identified as Parotid gland by proportion of serous vs mucous secretory acini.
questions.keyConcept: Parotid gland: Characteristic acinar composition.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Intralobular duct lined by simple columnar epithelium with basal striations (mitochondria packed between basal infoldings for electrolyte transport).
questions.keyConcept: Striated duct: Columnar cells with basal infoldings and mitochondria for sodium reabsorption.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Densely packed dark serous acini.
questions.keyConcept: Key identification criterion: Serous acini (Serous acini) — high-yield diagnostic spotter feature.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large excretory duct situated in interlobular connective tissue septa.
questions.keyConcept: Interlobular excretory duct.

questions.text: This section is taken from which gland?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Salivary gland identified as Submandibular gland by proportion of serous vs mucous secretory acini.
questions.keyConcept: Submandibular gland: Characteristic acinar composition.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Predominant serous acinar units.
questions.keyConcept: Serous secretory units.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Scattered pale mucous acini.
questions.keyConcept: Key identification criterion: Mucous acini (Mucous acini) — high-yield diagnostic spotter feature.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Dense collagenous septa subdividing the gland into lobules.
questions.keyConcept: Interlobular connective tissue.

questions.text: This section is taken from which gland?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Salivary gland identified as Sublingual gland by proportion of serous vs mucous secretory acini.
questions.keyConcept: Sublingual gland: Characteristic acinar composition.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Abundant pale mucous acinar units.
questions.keyConcept: Key identification criterion: Mucous units (Mucous acini) — high-yield diagnostic spotter feature.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Serous demilunes and acini.
questions.keyConcept: Key identification criterion: Serous units (Interlobular duct) — high-yield diagnostic spotter feature.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Interlobular septum.
questions.keyConcept: Interlobular septum.

questions.text: what type of epithelium makes up structure (2)
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Striated ducts are lined by simple columnar cells with basal striations.
questions.keyConcept: Striated duct epithelium: Simple columnar.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Prominent intralobular striated duct.
questions.keyConcept: Key identification criterion: Striated duct (Striated duct) — high-yield diagnostic spotter feature.

questions.text: This section is taken from which gland?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Salivary gland identified as Parotid gland by proportion of serous vs mucous secretory acini.
questions.keyConcept: Parotid gland: Characteristic acinar composition.

questions.text: What do the three lines on the right point to?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Purely serous secretory units of parotid gland.
questions.keyConcept: Parotid purely serous acini.

questions.text: What does the single line at the upper left point to?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Intralobular duct profile.
questions.keyConcept: Intralobular duct.

questions.text: This section is taken from which gland?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Salivary gland identified as Parotid gland by proportion of serous vs mucous secretory acini.
questions.keyConcept: Parotid gland: Characteristic acinar composition.

questions.text: What are the predominant secretory units shown?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Purely serous acini constitute 100% of parotid parenchyma.
questions.keyConcept: Parotid acinar composition.

questions.text: This section is taken from which gland?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Mixed gland with overwhelmingly predominant mucous acini and few serous demilunes.
questions.keyConcept: Sublingual gland: Mixed predominantly mucous.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Striated duct.
questions.keyConcept: Key identification criterion: Striated duct (Striated duct) — high-yield diagnostic spotter feature.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Lobule packed with pale-staining mucous acini.
questions.keyConcept: Key identification criterion: Mucous lobule (Lobule with mucous acini) — high-yield diagnostic spotter feature.

questions.text: Which structure is shown in this SEM photomicrograph?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) showing characteristic curved horn-like, keratinized filiform papillae.
questions.keyConcept: Filiform papillae on SEM: Tapered spires of keratinized epithelium.

questions.text: What is the structure outlined in yellow?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Taste bud outlined in yellow.
questions.keyConcept: Key identification criterion: Taste bud (Taste bud) — high-yield diagnostic spotter feature.

questions.keyConcept: Key identification criterion: Taste pore (Taste pore) — high-yield diagnostic spotter feature.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Elongated neuroepithelial sensory cells with central oval nuclei.
questions.keyConcept: Gustatory sensory cells.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Sustentacular supporting cells.
questions.keyConcept: Supporting cells of taste bud.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Short pyramidal stem cells at the base.
questions.keyConcept: Key identification criterion: Basal cells (Basal cells) — high-yield diagnostic spotter feature.

questions.text: The cell outlined in yellow belongs to which structure?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: TEM of serous acinar cell showing extensive parallel stacks of rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) in the basal region and dense apical zymogen granules.
questions.keyConcept: Ultrastructure of serous cell: Basal RER + apical electron-dense zymogen granules.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Dense zymogen granules packed in the apical cytoplasm.
questions.keyConcept: Key identification criterion: Zymogen granules (Apical electron dense granules) — high-yield diagnostic spotter feature.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Rounded euchromatic nucleus located basally.
questions.keyConcept: Serous cell nucleus.

questions.text: The cell outlined in yellow belongs to which structure?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: TEM of mucous cell showing abundant pale, electron-lucent mucinogen granules filling the supranuclear cytoplasm and flattening the basal nucleus.
questions.keyConcept: Ultrastructure of mucous cell: Electron-lucent mucin droplets + flattened basal nucleus.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Light, electron-lucent membrane-bound mucin droplets.
questions.keyConcept: Mucin droplets on TEM.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Flattened nucleus compressed against the basal plasma membrane.
questions.keyConcept: Flattened basal nucleus in mucous cells.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Apical acinar lumen.
questions.keyConcept: Key identification criterion: Lumen (Lumen of acinus) — high-yield diagnostic spotter feature.

questions.text: This section is taken from which structure?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Transverse section of the esophagus showing non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium, muscularis mucosae, submucosal esophageal glands proper, and muscularis externa.
questions.keyConcept: Esophageal wall layers.

questions.text: This section is taken from which structure?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Transverse section of the esophagus showing non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium, muscularis mucosae, submucosal esophageal glands proper, and muscularis externa.
questions.keyConcept: Esophageal wall layers.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Thick, non-keratinized stratified squamous lining protective against abrasion.
questions.keyConcept: Esophageal epithelium: Non-keratinized stratified squamous.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Connective tissue with blood vessels and lymphatics.
questions.keyConcept: Key identification criterion: Lamina propria (Lamina propria) — high-yield diagnostic spotter feature.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Distinct longitudinal layer of smooth muscle separating mucosa from submucosa.
questions.keyConcept: Muscularis mucosae of esophagus.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Compound tubuloacinar mucous glands situated exclusively in the submucosa.
questions.keyConcept: Esophageal glands proper (submucosal).

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Innermost layer (epithelium + lamina propria + muscularis mucosae).
questions.keyConcept: Key identification criterion: Mucosa (Mucosa) — high-yield diagnostic spotter feature.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Dense irregular connective tissue layer harboring submucosal glands.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Excretory duct lined by stratified cuboidal/columnar epithelium.
questions.keyConcept: Key identification criterion: Excretory duct (Duct) — high-yield diagnostic spotter feature.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Thick muscular coat.
questions.keyConcept: Muscularis externa.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Submucosal layer.
questions.keyConcept: Key identification criterion: Submucosa (Submucosa) — high-yield diagnostic spotter feature.

questions.text: Identify the cell shown in this TEM photo.
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: TEM of parietal (oxyntic) cell showing prominent intracellular secretory canaliculi lined by microvilli, extensive tubulovesicular system, and innumerable large mitochondria (supplying ATP for H+/K+ ATPase acid pump).
questions.keyConcept: Parietal cell ultrastructure: Intracellular canaliculi, tubulovesicular system, abundant mitochondria.

questions.text: Identify the cell shown in this TEM photo.
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: TEM of peptic (chief) cell demonstrating abundant parallel arrays of rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) in the basal cytoplasm and apical electron-dense zymogen granules containing pepsinogen.
questions.keyConcept: Chief cell ultrastructure: Extensive basal RER, supranuclear Golgi, apical zymogen granules.

questions.text: Identify the cell shown in this TEM photo.
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Closed enteroendocrine cell: rests on the basement membrane but does NOT reach the luminal surface; contains membrane-bound neurosecretory granules concentrated in the basal cytoplasm near capillary fenestrae.
questions.keyConcept: Closed enteroendocrine cell: Does not contact lumen; basal endocrine granules.

questions.text: Identify the cell shown in this TEM photo.
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Open enteroendocrine cell: has a narrow apical cytoplasmic process equipped with microvilli reaching the intestinal lumen to sample luminal chemical contents (chemoreceptor).
questions.keyConcept: Open enteroendocrine cell: Apical process contacts lumen (luminal chemosensor).

questions.text: Identify the cell shown in this TEM photo.
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Pyramidal cell situated at the base of intestinal crypts containing large, brightly refractile apical secretory granules rich in lysozyme, defensins, and zinc.
questions.keyConcept: Paneth cell: Base of crypts, large apical eosinophilic antibacterial granules.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Gastric mucosa identified as Fundus by pit-to-gland ratio and cellular composition (fundus has shallow pits and straight glands packed with parietal and chief cells; pylorus has deep pits >1/2 mucosal thickness and branched coiled mucous glands).

questions.text: What is the diagnosis of the arrowed lesion?
options: Dilated, tortuous veins bulging under the esophageal mucosa
Dilated, tortuous lymphatics bulging under the esophageal mucosa
Elongated, tortuous arteries bulging under the gastric mucosa
Elongated, ulcerated veins projecting into the gastric lumen
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Lower end of esophagus opened longitudinally showing multiple prominent, bluish, elongated, tortuous, dilated submucosal veins bulging beneath the mucosal surface, characteristic of esophageal varices.
questions.keyConcept: Esophageal varices: Submucosal venous tortuosity at the lower third of the esophagus due to portal hypertension (porto-systemic shunting).

options: Thickened longitudinal mucosal folds of the lower esophagus
Dilated, elongated, tortuous veins under the esophageal mucosa
Linear ulcers along the lower esophageal mucosa
Fibrous bands crossing the lower esophageal mucosa
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The arrows indicate the dilated, elongated, and tortuous submucosal veins running longitudinally in the lower third of the esophagus.
questions.keyConcept: Esophageal varices: Longitudinal tortuous submucosal venous cords.

questions.text: All of the following are effects of liver cirrhosis EXCEPT:
options: Oesophageal varices at the lower end of the oesophagus
Enlarged, congested spleen with a thick capsule
Dark red spleen with atrophic white pulp
Thickened, fibrosed white portal tracts in the liver
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: All are consequences of liver cirrhosis and chronic venous congestion of the portal system except atrophic white pulp with dark red appearance. In chronic congestive splenomegaly (Banti's disease), the spleen is markedly enlarged and firm with a thick fibrous capsule; cut section shows prominent trabeculae and fibrosis (Gandy-Gamna bodies), not atrophy.
questions.keyConcept: Congestive splenomegaly: Markedly enlarged, firm spleen with thickened capsule and fibrocongestive red pulp expansion.

options: Chronic peptic ulcer of the stomach
Acute gastric erosion of the stomach
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Stomach opened to reveal a solitary, rounded, sharply punched-out ulcer on the lesser curvature of the prepyloric region. The mucosal folds (rugae) radiate symmetrically towards the margins of the ulcer, and the floor is clean and indurated, pathognomonic of a chronic benign peptic ulcer.
questions.keyConcept: Chronic peptic ulcer: Solitary, punched-out mucosal defect with radiating rugae and clean fibrotic base.

questions.text: The orange arrow points to the mucosa around the ulcer. It appears:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: In chronic peptic ulcers, the surrounding mucosa is flattened and smooth, with mucosal rugae radiating towards the ulcer crater due to cicatricial contraction of fibrous tissue in the base.
questions.keyConcept: Peptic ulcer gross margin: Smooth, flat margin with radiating rugae.

questions.text: All of the following describe this ulcer EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: A hard, wide, infiltrating base is the hallmark of a malignant ulcer (gastric adenocarcinoma). Chronic peptic ulcers feature a sharply punched-out, clean or scarred base limited to the muscularis propria without diffuse infiltration.
questions.keyConcept: Malignant vs benign gastric ulcer: Hard infiltrating base characterizes carcinoma.

options: Chronic peptic ulcer of the pylorus
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Segment of stomach showing marked circumferential mural thickening of the pyloric canal with rigidity and luminal stenosis (napkin-ring / linitis plastica type of infiltrating adenocarcinoma).
questions.keyConcept: Infiltrating pyloric carcinoma: Diffuse circumferential mural thickening causing gastric outlet obstruction.

options: Chronic peptic ulcer of the pylorus
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Segment of stomach showing marked circumferential mural thickening of the pyloric canal with rigidity and luminal stenosis (napkin-ring / linitis plastica type of infiltrating adenocarcinoma).
questions.keyConcept: Infiltrating pyloric carcinoma: Diffuse circumferential mural thickening causing gastric outlet obstruction.

options: Marked circumferential thickening of the pyloric wall by greyish tumour tissue
Marked circumferential thickening of the pyloric wall by whitish fibrous tissue
Marked localized thickening of the pyloric wall by greyish tumour tissue
Marked localized thickening of the gastric body wall by whitish fibrous tissue
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label 3 indicates the marked circumferential thickening of the pyloric wall by infiltrative, greyish-white malignant tumor tissue.
questions.keyConcept: Pyloric adenocarcinoma: Circumferential greyish-white mural infiltration.

options: Mucosal infiltration; marked dilatation of the lumen
Muscle infiltration; marked narrowing of the lumen
Muscle infiltration; marked dilatation of the lumen
Serosal infiltration; marked narrowing of the lumen
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label 1 shows diffuse infiltration of the muscularis externa by malignant scirrhous carcinoma, and Label 2 demonstrates severe stenosis (narrowing) of the pyloric lumen.
questions.keyConcept: Linitis plastica / Scirrhous carcinoma: Muscular infiltration producing concentric luminal stenosis.

options: Malignant ulcer of the stomach with gastrojejunostomy
Infiltrating carcinoma of the stomach with gastrojejunostomy
Malignant ulcer of the duodenum with gastroduodenostomy
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Museum jar displaying a segment of stomach with a chronic peptic ulcer anastomosed surgically to an adjacent loop of jejunum (gastrojejunostomy) created to bypass gastric outlet obstruction.
questions.keyConcept: Gastrojejunostomy: Surgical bypass anastomosis between stomach and proximal jejunum for obstructed peptic ulcer.

questions.text: Q13. Labels A, B and C represent respectively:
options: Large ulcer at the pyloric region; opened duodenum and jejunum; normal gastric rugae
Large ulcer at the cardiac region; opened duodenum and jejunum; flattened gastric rugae
Large ulcer at the pyloric region; opened duodenum and ileum; lost gastric rugae
Small ulcer at the pyloric region; opened jejunum and ileum; normal gastric rugae
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Gross pathology shows a chronic peptic ulcer at the prepyloric region with surgical gastrojejunostomy.
questions.keyConcept: Peptic ulcer with surgical anastomosis.

questions.text: The circled lesion is located at the:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The chronic peptic ulcer is located prepylorically along the lesser curvature.
questions.keyConcept: Gastric ulcer location: Commonly lesser curvature and prepyloric antrum.

questions.text: The  arrow on the right points to:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Mucosal rugae adjacent to the anastomotic stoma are flattened.
questions.keyConcept: Mucosal changes in chronic peptic disease.

options: Raised everted edge; necrotic floor; hard infiltrating base
Flat clear-cut edge; necrotic floor; soft fibrous base
Raised everted edge; clean floor; hard infiltrating base
Flat undermined edge; clean floor; soft fibrous base
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The classic triad of a malignant ulcer (gastric carcinoma): (1) raised everted (rolled-out) margins, (2) necrotic, irregular, hemorrhagic floor, and (3) hard, indurated, deeply infiltrating base.
questions.keyConcept: Triad of malignant ulcer: Raised everted edges, necrotic dirty floor, hard infiltrating base.

questions.text: All of the following are true except  EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: A sharply punched-out outline is characteristic of a benign chronic peptic ulcer. Malignant ulcers have irregular, raised, everted margins with diffuse invasion.
questions.keyConcept: Malignant ulcer: Irregular outline with rolled-out edges, not punched-out.

options: Jejunum attached to the duodenum with an artificial opening between their lumina
Jejunum attached to the stomach with an artificial opening between their lumina
Duodenum attached to the stomach with a natural opening between their lumina
Jejunum attached to the stomach with a fistulous tract between their lumina
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Gastrojejunostomy consists of an artificial surgical stoma created between the dependent portion of the greater curvature of the stomach and a loop of proximal jejunum.
questions.keyConcept: Gastrojejunostomy: Surgical stoma connecting gastric and jejunal lumina.

questions.text: THis lesion is best characterized as:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Well-defined, solitary crater with dense fibrous base and radiating rugae, diagnostic of a chronic peptic ulcer.
questions.keyConcept: Chronic peptic ulcer.

questions.text: All of the following are true about the ulcer  EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Chronic peptic ulcers do NOT have an extensive hard infiltrating base; that finding signifies gastric adenocarcinoma.
questions.keyConcept: Benign peptic ulcer features.

options: Chronic peptic ulcer with surrounding fibrosis
Infiltrating carcinoma of the pylorus only
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large, irregular ulcer with prominent raised, rolled, everted margins and a necrotic slough in the floor, diagnostic of ulcerating gastric adenocarcinoma.
questions.keyConcept: Gastric adenocarcinoma: Malignant ulceration.

options: Chronic peptic ulcer of the stomach
Acute gastric ulcer of the stomach
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large ulcerative lesion with characteristic malignant features: everted boundaries and necrotic base.
questions.keyConcept: Malignant gastric ulcer.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label 1 points to the raised, everted (rolled) tumor margin, while label 2 points to the necrotic, hemorrhagic, dirty floor of the ulcer.
questions.keyConcept: Malignant ulcer morphology.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Liver surface is distorted by large, irregular regenerating nodules measuring between 0.5 cm and 3 cm in diameter, separated by broad bands of depressed fibrous tissue, characteristic of macronodular (post-hepatitic) cirrhosis.
questions.keyConcept: Macronodular cirrhosis: Coarse regenerating nodules (>3 mm, up to 2–3 cm) separated by irregular fibrous scars (viral hepatitis B/C etiology).

questions.text: Label 2 points to the nodules. They are:
options: Multiple, round, less than 3 mm in diameter
Multiple, round, 0.5 to 2 cm in diameter
multiple, round, about 5 cm in diameter
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The nodules in macronodular cirrhosis are large, varying from 0.5 to 2 cm in diameter.
questions.keyConcept: Nodule dimensions in macronodular cirrhosis.

options: Low hills and shallow depressions of capsule
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The Glisson's capsule of the cirrhotic liver is chronically thickened and fibrotic.
questions.keyConcept: Capsular thickening in cirrhosis.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Prominent large nodules separated by broad fibrous depressions.
questions.keyConcept: Macronodular cirrhosis.

questions.text: All of the following are features of this liver EXCEPT:
options: Markedly shrunken with retracted cut section
Normal liver tissue in between the nodules
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: In macronodular cirrhosis, the fibrous bands are broad, irregular, and depressed between the regenerating parenchyma.
questions.keyConcept: Fibrous septa in macronodular cirrhosis.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Cirrhotic liver containing a massive, dominant, yellowish-white, necrotic tumor mass with satellite nodules, representing hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) arising as a complication of cirrhosis.
questions.keyConcept: Hepatocellular carcinoma: Arises on top of HBV/HCV macronodular cirrhosis.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Background of regenerating cirrhotic nodules with a superimposed large neoplastic tumor mass.
questions.keyConcept: HCC complicating cirrhosis.

questions.text: All of the following describe the spleen in  EXCEPT
options: Dark red with atrophic white pulp
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label 1 points to the main HCC tumor mass, which is bulky, unencapsulated, and shows typical variegated cut surface with areas of yellow necrosis and dark hemorrhage.
questions.keyConcept: Gross features of hepatocellular carcinoma.

options: Laennec’s cirrhosis with nodular cut section
Macronodular cirrhosis with nodular cut section
Bilharzial fibrosis with white portal tracts
Fatty change with yellow bulging surface
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label 2 indicates the background cirrhotic regenerative nodules.
questions.keyConcept: Cirrhotic nodules.

questions.text: All of the following are true about the specimens  EXCEPT:
options: The esophagus shows dilated tortuous submucosal veins
The liver shows thickened white portal tracts
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Liver cut section displaying broad, dense, whitish fibrous collars expanding the portal tracts around portal vein branches resembling the stems of clay pipes ('pipe-stem fibrosis'). Liver lobular architecture is preserved, and true regenerative nodules are absent.
questions.keyConcept: Symmers' pipe-stem fibrosis: Periportal fibrosis around intrahepatic portal branches with preserved parenchymal lobules (non-cirrhotic portal hypertension).

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Dense white fibrous sheaths surrounding portal tracts.
questions.keyConcept: Pipe-stem fibrosis.

questions.text: All of the following describe the arrowed mass EXCEPT:
options: Greyish with areas of haemorrhage and necrosis
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The white bands are thick sleeves of collagenous scar tissue expanding the portal triads.
questions.keyConcept: Periportal fibrous cuffs in schistosomiasis.

options: Cirrhotic nodules in a macronodular cirrhosis
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Hepatic parenchyma between the pipe-stem fibrous tracts shows preserved architectural lobulation without pseudolobules.
questions.keyConcept: Preserved lobular architecture in Bilharzial fibrosis.

questions.text: The tissue between the nodules is
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: In Schistosoma mansoni pipe-stem fibrosis, the normal lobular architecture of the liver is preserved, distinguishing it from true cirrhosis.
questions.keyConcept: Non-cirrhotic portal fibrosis.

options: Cirrhotic nodules in a macronodular cirrhosis
Cirrhotic nodules in a micronodular cirrhosis
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: All are true EXCEPT impaired liver functions. In Schistosoma pipe-stem fibrosis, hepatocellular synthetic function (albumin, coagulation factors) is preserved until very late, because the hepatocytes themselves are not destroyed.
questions.keyConcept: Preserved hepatocellular function in Bilharzial hepatic fibrosis.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Liver enlarged and studded with multiple, bilateral, spherical, whitish-tan tumor deposits of varying sizes, many displaying central necrosis and umbilication (central depression), pathognomonic of hematogenous hepatic metastases.
questions.keyConcept: Hepatic metastases: Multiple, variable-sized, bilateral spherical nodules with central umbilication.

options: Multiple, irregular, filled with necrotic liver tissue
Multiple, regular, with thick fibrous walls
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Multiple cannonball nodules scattered throughout both liver lobes.
questions.keyConcept: Metastatic liver disease.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The central depression in metastatic nodules results from rapid tumor outgrowth of its blood supply, causing ischemic central necrosis and retraction.
questions.keyConcept: Central umbilication in liver metastases.

questions.text: The cavity wall is lined by:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Key diagnostic hallmark: multiplicity, size variation, and central umbilication.
questions.keyConcept: Gross criteria of secondary liver tumors.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Gallbladder opened to reveal a markedly thickened, fibrotic, greyish-white wall and an inflamed mucosal surface containing multiple faceted, yellow-brown gallstones (cholelithiasis).
questions.keyConcept: Chronic calculous cholecystitis: Thick fibrotic wall with multiple faceted gallstones.

options: Thick fibrous wall with chalky white calcification
Thick fibrous wall with irregular necrotic lining
Thin fibrous wall with chalky white calcification
Thin fibrous wall with smooth regular lining
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Classic museum specimen of chronic gallstone disease.
questions.keyConcept: Calculous cholecystitis.

questions.text: The border of this liver is described as:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The wall of the gallbladder is abnormally thickened (often >4-5 mm) by dense fibrous scar tissue.
questions.keyConcept: Mural fibrosis in chronic cholecystitis.

options: Portal tracts that are thickened, fibrosed and white
Portal tracts that are thickened, fibrosed and yellow
Dilated bile ducts with surrounding fibrosis
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The stones are multiple with flat, polished facet surfaces resulting from mutual friction and compression within the contracted gallbladder.
questions.keyConcept: Faceted gallstones: Mixed stones formed by chronic cholelithiasis and friction.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: A thin, translucent wall is normal. Chronic cholecystitis causes dense, thick, opaque, fibrotic mural hypertrophy.
questions.keyConcept: Features of chronic cholecystitis.

questions.text: The liver tissue between the portal tracts is greyish brown because of:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Gallbladder with a thick, contracted wall harboring a solitary, large, rounded, barrel-shaped cholesterol gallstone.
questions.keyConcept: Solitary pure cholesterol gallstone in chronic cholecystitis.

questions.text: All of the following describe these nodules EXCEPT:
options: Separated by fibrous bands with no normal live
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The single stone is large, yellowish, oval, with a smooth surface.
questions.keyConcept: Cholesterol stone morphology.

questions.keyConcept: Adenoma-carcinoma sequence.

questions.text: identify the structure indicated by the right arrow.
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Arrows demonstrate elongated, dark, hyperchromatic nuclei stacked upon one another (pseudostratification), typical of low-grade dysplasia.
questions.keyConcept: Cytological features of low-grade dysplasia.

questions.text: A histopathological examination of a colonic tumor reveals malignant glands of variable size and shape. The glands are lined by one or more layers of malignant cells and invade through the basement membrane into the submucosa.
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Arrow points to the adjacent normal colonic mucosa with straight crypts and abundant goblet cells.
questions.keyConcept: Normal colonic crypt architecture.

questions.text: What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Irregular, crowded, infiltrative malignant glands invading through the muscularis mucosae into the submucosa, lined by pleomorphic, hyperchromatic malignant cells, diagnostic of invasive adenocarcinoma.
questions.keyConcept: Colorectal adenocarcinoma: Malignant glands infiltrating through muscularis mucosae.

questions.text: All of the following are true about this legion EXCEPT:
options: It may present with bleeding per rectum.
It may present with irregular bowel habits.
It may appear as an ulcerating, fungating or infiltrating mass.
Its malignant glands may invade the submucosa.
Its epithelial cells show no nuclear atypia.
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Irregular, crowded, infiltrative malignant glands invading through the muscularis mucosae into the submucosa, lined by pleomorphic, hyperchromatic malignant cells, diagnostic of invasive adenocarcinoma.
questions.keyConcept: Colorectal adenocarcinoma: Malignant glands infiltrating through muscularis mucosae.

questions.text: All of the following are characteristic microscopic features of this legion EXCEPT:
options: Glands variable in size and shape
Cystically dilated glands lined by bland columnar
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: All are true EXCEPT absence of nuclear atypia. Colorectal adenocarcinoma cells ALWAYS display marked cytological atypia, pleomorphism, and atypical mitoses.
questions.keyConcept: Malignant cytological atypia.

questions.text: Autoinfection is a recognized means of transmission of this parasite. Yes or No? Justify.
options: No - the egg must pass through a snail intermediate host
No - the egg must embryonate in moist soil for 2-3 weeks before it is infective
Yes - the larva inside the egg becomes infective within about 6 hours on the perianal skin, and scratching carries eggs to the mouth
Yes - rhabditiform larvae become filariform larvae inside the intestine
Yes - the egg hatches in the colon and the larva penetrates the colonic wall
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Enterobius vermicularis (pinworm) eggs are laid on the perianal skin by nocturnal migrating gravid females. The coiled tadpole-like larva develops into the infective third-stage larva within only 4 to 6 hours at body temperature, allowing retrofection or external autoinfection via contaminated fingers after scratching.
questions.keyConcept: Enterobius vermicularis autoinfection: Rapid perianal embryonation in 6 hours enables direct fecal-oral autoinfection.

questions.text: This worm came out through the nose of a child after general anesthesia. Which figure represents the stage found on his stool examination?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Migration of adult Ascaris lumbricoides through the mouth or nose is a classic feature of anesthesia or pyrexia. Figure A represents the fertilized Ascaris egg: golden-brown, broadly oval, surrounded by a thick, bile-stained, coarsely mammillated albuminous coat containing an unsegmented ovum.
questions.keyConcept: Ascaris lumbricoides: Adult erratic migration; stool shows characteristic mammillated fertilized eggs.

questions.text: Rectal prolapse is a complication of heavy infection with this worm. Interpret.
options: Chronic blood loss causes atrophy of the anal sphincter
Gravid females migrate out at night, causing straining during sleep
A bolus of entangled adult worms obstructs the rectum and pushes it outwards
Flask-shaped ulcers weaken the rectal wall
The worm is deeply embedded in the mucosa by its thin anterior part, causing loss of muscle tone in heavy infection
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: In heavy Trichuris trichiura (whipworm) infection (Trichuris dysentery syndrome), thousands of worms thread their attenuated anterior two-thirds into the cecal and rectal mucosa, eliciting chronic inflammation, loss of muscle tone, and tenesmus leading to rectal prolapse.
questions.keyConcept: Trichuris trichiura: Attenuated anterior end threads into colonic mucosa, precipitating rectal prolapse in children.

questions.text: A patient has hepatomegaly and jaundice. Three months ago he had fever, right upper quadrant pain and eosinophilia after eating green salads. Which figure represents the stage found on stool examination?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Ingestion of green salads contaminated with encysted metacercariae leads to acute fascioliasis (biliary colic, high fever, eosinophilia, tender hepatomegaly). The diagnostic stage on stool examination is the Fasciola egg: large (140 x 80 µm), ellipsoidal, yellowish-brown, operculated, containing an unsegmented ovum surrounded by yolk cells.
questions.keyConcept: Fasciola hepatica: Transmitted via encysted metacercariae on watercress; large operculated unsegmented egg.

questions.text: Identify the station and what this stage does after leaving the snail:
options: Leptocercus cercaria of Heterophyes - encysts in fish muscle
Leptocercus cercaria of Fasciola - penetrates human skin
Furcocercus cercaria of Schistosoma - encysts on aquatic plants
Furcocercus cercaria of Schistosoma - penetrates human skin
Leptocercus cercaria of Fasciola - encysts on aquatic plants as a metacercaria
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Fasciola cercaria (leptocercus cercaria) has a simple, unbranched tail and dark cystogenous glands. Upon emergence from the Lymnaea snail, it encysts on emergent aquatic vegetation (watercress) to form the infective encysted metacercaria.
questions.keyConcept: Fasciola cercaria: Leptocercus (simple tail), encysts on aquatic plants as metacercaria.

questions.text: Identify the station and the arrowed part:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Adult Echinococcus granulosus measures 3–6 mm and consists of only 3 proglottids: immature, mature, and a large terminal gravid segment (which occupies more than half of the total worm length and contains a branched sac-like uterus filled with eggs).
questions.keyConcept: Echinococcus granulosus adult: 3 segments (immature, mature, gravid); gravid segment > half total worm length.

questions.text: Autoinfection is a means of transmission of this parasite. Yes or No? Justify.
options: No - the egg must embryonate in soil for weeks
Yes - the egg is infective when passed and can hatch in the intestine, where the oncosphere develops into a cysticercoid in the villi
Yes - rhabditiform larvae become filariform larvae in the intestine
Yes - the egg needs about 6 hours on the perianal skin before it becomes infective
No - an insect intermediate host is always needed
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Hymenolepis nana (dwarf tapeworm) is the only human cestode capable of internal autoinfection: eggs released in the small intestine can hatch prematurely, releasing hexacanth oncospheres that invade the villi to develop into cysticercoids without exiting the host.
questions.keyConcept: Hymenolepis nana: Only cestode with direct internal autoinfection (cysticercoids develop within intestinal villi).

questions.text: In this cyst aspirate, the arrowed structures are the hooks of:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Hydatid sand examined microscopically consists of free hooklets, calcareous corpuscles, and invaginated protoscolices displaying a double row of hooklets and 4 suckers.
questions.keyConcept: Hydatid sand: Protoscolices with characteristic double-crowned hooklets and suckers.

questions.text: Food handlers are a serious source of this infection. Yes or No? Justify.
options: No - the infection is transmitted only through water
No - the cyst must mature in soil before it becomes infective
Yes - asymptomatic carriers pass mature quadrinucleate cysts that are infective on passage and contaminate food
Yes - trophozoites survive on food and invade the colon
No - only trophozoites are passed, and they die quickly outside the body
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Food handlers shedding mature 4-nucleated Entamoeba histolytica or Giardia cysts are a major source of infection because the cysts are immediately infective upon passage, resistant to environmental chlorination, and easily transmitted via contaminated hands.
questions.keyConcept: Amebiasis & Giardiasis: Asymptomatic cyst passers serve as key epidemiologic reservoirs.

questions.text: Identify the adult worm and how it causes internal autoinfection:
options: Echinococcus granulosus - a ruptured hydatid cyst releases protoscolices that grow into adults
Diphyllobothrium latum - plerocercoids develop in the intestinal wall
Taenia saginata - reverse peristalsis carries gravid segments to the stomach
Hymenolepis nana - eggs hatch in the intestine and oncospheres develop into cysticercoids in the villi
Hymenolepis nana - it does not cause autoinfection; a flea or beetle intermediate host is obligatory
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Hymenolepis nana adult worm causes internal autoinfection when retained eggs hatch in the lumen and develop into tissue cysticercoids in the villi.
questions.keyConcept: Hymenolepis nana internal autoinfection mechanism.

questions.text: Structure 3 in this specimen is the:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Structure 3 is the gynecophoric canal of the male Schistosoma: a ventral longitudinal groove formed by inrolled lateral margins extending from the ventral sucker to the posterior extremity, inside which the slender female is embraced.
questions.keyConcept: Male Schistosoma gynecophoric canal: Ventral groove embracing female worm.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Scolex is cuboidal (1–2 mm in diameter), possesses 4 prominent hemispherical suckers, but completely lacks a rostellum and lacks hooks (unarmed scolex).
questions.keyConcept: Taenia saginata scolex: 4 suckers, NO rostellum, NO hooks (unarmed).

questions.text: Structure 2 in this specimen is composed of:
options: Numerous follicular testes scattered in the body
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Male Schistosoma mansoni possesses 6 to 9 testes clustered in a compact zigzag mass situated dorsally behind the ventral sucker.
questions.keyConcept: Male Schistosoma mansoni: 6–9 testes clustered in a mass.

questions.text: Identify the egg and its arrowed content:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Male Schistosoma haematobium has 4-5 testes, while Heterophyes has 2 oval testes; male Schistosoma with testes arranged in a line.
questions.keyConcept: Schistosoma testicular anatomy.

questions.text: The middle arrow points to a structure that distinguishes this fluke from Metagonimus yokogawai. It is the:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Minute pyriform fluke (1.5 mm) with 3 suckers (oral sucker, ventral sucker, and a prominent genital sucker / gonotyl armed with 70–80 chitinous spinelets).
questions.keyConcept: Heterophyes heterophyes: Minute fluke characterized by a third sucker (genital sucker / gonotyl).

questions.text: Finding this egg in a single stool sample does not always mean active infection. Interpret.
options: The egg is a degenerated form that has lost its operculum
The egg is shed only in the acute (invasive) stage of the disease
The egg may pass transiently after eating infected raw liver , so stool is re-examined after a liver-free diet
The egg is shed only in bile, so duodenal aspirate is needed
The egg is identical to the Heterophyes egg, so serology is required
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large leaf-like fluke (up to 7 cm long) with parallel lateral margins, weakly developed cephalic cone, deeply branched intestinal caeca, and highly branched testes.
questions.keyConcept: Fasciola gigantica: Large fluke with parallel margins, indistinct shoulders, and branched caeca.

questions.text: Autoinfection is a means of transmission of this parasite. Yes or No? Justify.
options: No - infection occurs only by skin penetration by filariform larvae
Yes - the egg hatches in the colon and the larvae re-invade the mucosa
No - man is only an accidental host of this worm
No - the egg is passed with an unsegmented ovum and must embryonate in soil before it becomes infective
Yes - the mucoid plugs dissolve on the perianal skin and release infective larvae
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Modified Ziehl-Neelsen (Kinyoun) acid-fast stain showing bright pinkish-red, spherical, acid-fast oocysts measuring 4–5 µm against a blue-green background.
questions.keyConcept: Cryptosporidium parvum: Acid-fast spherical oocysts (4–5 µm) on modified ZN stain.

questions.text: A 31-year-old HIV-infected woman presents with severe watery diarrhea and dizziness. Which figure represents the stage found on stool examination?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: In HIV/AIDS patients with CD4 < 100, Cryptosporidium parvum causes cholera-like, profuse, secretory watery diarrhea leading to fatal dehydration. The acid-fast stain reveals characteristic spherical pink-red oocysts.
questions.keyConcept: Cryptosporidiosis in AIDS: Intractable secretory watery diarrhea; diagnosed by acid-fast oocysts.

questions.text: Which of these stages can cause internal autoinfection, so that the whole life cycle is completed inside one human host?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Stage capable of internal autoinfection causing persistent hyperinfection.
questions.keyConcept: Internal autoinfection in parasitology.

questions.text: Identify the station and the arrowed structure:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large leaf-shaped fluke (3 cm) with distinct conical cephalic projection and prominent triangular shoulders.
questions.keyConcept: Fasciola hepatica: Distinct cephalic cone and prominent shoulders.

questions.text: Identify the station and the main reservoir of infection:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Active motility by rapid progressive unidirectional pseudopodia, single vesicular nucleus with central pinpoint karyosome, and ingested red blood cells (erythrophagocytosis, pathognomonic of invasive amebiasis).
questions.keyConcept: Entamoeba histolytica trophozoite: Erythrophagocytosis and central karyosome.

questions.text: This parasite causes flask-shaped intestinal ulcers and extra-intestinal manifestations. Interpret.
options: Trophozoites lyse the mucosa with proteolytic enzymes, spread laterally in the submucosa, and reach the liver through the portal vein
Eggs lodge in the bowel wall and cause granulomas that ulcerate
Adult worms embed their anterior ends deep in the mucosa
Trophozoites burrow with their cilia and invade the lymphatics
Cysts excyst in the submucosa and grow into large colonies
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Pear-shaped (tennis racket-shaped), bilateral symmetry, 2 large suction discs (adhesive discs), 2 nuclei ('face-like' appearance), and 4 pairs of flagella with falling-leaf motility.
questions.keyConcept: Giardia lamblia trophozoite: Bilateral symmetry, 2 nuclei, 2 sucking discs, falling-leaf motility.

questions.text: The snail that harbors the larval stages of this parasite is:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Oval shape, smooth thick cyst wall, 4 nuclei (often grouped at one pole), curved parabasal bodies, and longitudinal axonemes.
questions.keyConcept: Giardia lamblia cyst: Oval, 4 nuclei, axostyle and curved parabasal bodies.

questions.text: Identify the station and the arrowed structure:
options: Entamoeba histolytica cyst - nucleus with central karyosome
Entamoeba histolytica trophozoite - nucleus with central karyosome
Entamoeba coli trophozoite - nucleus with eccentric karyosome
Entamoeba coli trophozoite - nucleus with central karyosome
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Spherical cyst (10–15 µm) containing 1 to 4 nuclei with central pinpoint karyosomes, and cigar-shaped chromatoid bars with rounded ends.
questions.keyConcept: Entamoeba histolytica mature cyst: Spherical, 4 nuclei, cigar-shaped chromatoid bodies.

questions.text: Which feature distinguishes this fluke from Fasciola spp.?
options: Separate sexes with a gynecophoric canal
Branched intestinal caeca with a cephalic cone
Simple, unbranched intestinal caeca and no cephalic cone
A genital sucker beside the ventral sucker
A ventral sucker displaced to one side
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Scolex equipped with 4 suckers and a rounded rostellum armed with a double crown of 22 to 32 alternating large and small hooks (armed scolex).
questions.keyConcept: Taenia solium scolex: 4 suckers + rostellum with double crown of hooklets (armed).

questions.text: Identify the egg and the source of infection:
options: Heterophyes heterophyes egg - raw or undercooked fish
Fasciola egg - raw or undercooked fish
Heterophyes heterophyes egg - aquatic plants such as watercress
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Elongated rectangular segment (longer than broad) with a central median longitudinal uterine stem giving off 15 to 30 fine, dichotomously branched lateral uterine branches on each side.
questions.keyConcept: Taenia saginata gravid segment: 15–30 lateral uterine branches (dichotomous branching).

questions.text: A 4-year-old child has diarrhea with pale, loose, offensive, fatty stools and no mucus or blood. Which figure represents the stage found in a fresh diarrheic stool?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Giardiasis causes malabsorption syndrome with pale, greasy, foul-smelling diarrhea (steatorrhea) due to mechanical carpeting of the duodenal brush border. Figure represents the characteristic Giardia trophozoite/cyst.
questions.keyConcept: Giardiasis: Duodenal brush border carpeting causing malabsorptive steatorrhea.

questions.text: This parasite can be transmitted to humans by autoinfection. Yes or No? Justify.
options: No - this parasite infects only by larval skin penetration
Yes - the egg is infective on passage and is carried from the anus to the mouth
No - the egg can only infect after passing through Cyclops
Yes - the egg hatches in the small intestine and the larva migrates through the lungs again
No - the egg is passed with a one-cell ovum and needs about 2-3 weeks in soil to become embryonated
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Gravid segment containing 7 to 12 coarse, dendritic, laterally branched uterine branches on each side.
questions.keyConcept: Taenia solium gravid segment: 7–12 coarse lateral uterine branches.

questions.text: Identify the station and its identifying criterion:
options: Entamoeba coli cyst - up to 8 nuclei with eccentric karyosomes
Entamoeba histolytica cyst - 1-4 nuclei with central karyosomes
Giardia lamblia cyst - 4 nuclei and axostyles
Entamoeba histolytica cyst - up to 8 nuclei with central karyosomes
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Broader than long proglottid featuring a central rosette-shaped (coiled loop) uterus opening independently through a uterine pore.
questions.keyConcept: Diphyllobothrium latum: Proglottid broader than long with central rosette-shaped uterus.

questions.text: The arrowed structure in this larva is the:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Slender cylindrical nematode with a curved anterior end and a prominent posterior umbrella-like copulatory bursa supported by 14 rays.
questions.keyConcept: Male Ancylostoma duodenale: Copulatory bursa supported by rays.

questions.text: Perianal swabbing is the method of choice for diagnosing infection with this egg. Interpret.
options: The eggs are very light and are lost from the surface of the stool sample
The gravid female migrates out of the anus at night and lays her eggs on the perianal skin,
Larvae from these eggs penetrate the perianal skin and stay there
The eggs hatch inside the colon, so only larvae reach the stool
The eggs are digested by colonic bacteria before they are passed
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Tapered posterior end lacking a copulatory bursa, with vulva located near the junction of middle and posterior thirds.
questions.keyConcept: Female Ancylostoma duodenale: Conical tapered tail.

questions.text: Identify the specimen and the feature indicated by the lower arrow:
options: Strongyloides stercoralis female - tapering posterior end
Trichocephalus trichiurus female - blunt posterior end
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Small white spindle-shaped worm (8–13 mm) with cephalic cuticular alae and a long, sharply pointed, pin-like tail.
questions.keyConcept: Female Enterobius vermicularis: Pointed pin-like tail and cephalic alae.

options: Female of Strongyloides stercoralis with eggs in uterus
Female of Enterobius vermicularis with eggs in uterus
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large roundworm (15–30 cm) with a ventrally curved posterior extremity equipped with two copulatory spicules.
questions.keyConcept: Male Ascaris lumbricoides: Ventrally curved tail with 2 copulatory spicules.

questions.text: Identify the station. Why can man harbor this stage?
options: Cysticercus cellulosae - man can act as an intermediate host
Cysticercus cellulosae - man is infected only by eating undercooked pork
Cysticercus bovis - reverse peristalsis brings gravid segments to the stomach
Hydatid cyst - man swallows eggs from dog feces
Cysticercus bovis - man is the normal intermediate host
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large roundworm (20–40 cm) with a straight, conical posterior extremity and genital girdle.
questions.keyConcept: Female Ascaris lumbricoides: Straight tail, larger body.

questions.text: This parasitic stage represents the infective stage of a case of:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Classic whip-like morphology: attenuated, hair-like anterior three-fifths containing a stichosome cellular esophagus, and a thickened posterior two-fifths.
questions.keyConcept: Trichuris trichiura: Whip-like shape with thin anterior and stout posterior body.

questions.text: A 4-year-old child has pruritus ani, insomnia and nocturnal enuresis. Which figure represents the stage recovered by perianal swab?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Nocturnal pruritus ani and enuresis in children are diagnostic of Enterobius vermicularis. Figure represents the plano-convex D-shaped egg containing a folded larva.
questions.keyConcept: Enterobius vermicularis: Nocturnal perianal pruritus; D-shaped asymmetric egg.

questions.text: An abdominal CT of a shepherd with right upper abdominal pain and no fever shows multiple cystic lesions of different sizes in both liver lobes. Which figure represents the stage found when the cyst fluid is examined?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Shepherd with hepatic hydatid cyst (Echinococcus granulosus). Diagnostic stage is the hydatid sand containing protoscolices with double hooklet crowns.
questions.keyConcept: Echinococcus granulosus: Hepatic hydatid cyst in sheep-raising regions.

questions.text: An Egyptian farmer presented with hematemesis, hepatosplenomegaly and ascites. Sonography showed severe periportal fibrosis. Which figure represents the stage found on stool examination during the acute stage?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Farmer with portal hypertension, splenomegaly, and esophageal variceal bleeding due to Schistosoma mansoni. Diagnostic stage is the large oval egg with a sharp, prominent lateral spine.
questions.keyConcept: Schistosoma mansoni: Lateral-spined egg causing periportal fibrosis and hematemesis.

questions.text: Chronic blood loss in this infection is multifactorial. Interpret.
options: The worm competes with the host for vitamin B12 and folate in the jejunum
The worm sucks blood, and leaving bleeding points
Larvae damage the lung capillaries, causing repeated hemoptysis
Larvae migrate through the liver, causing bleeding esophageal varices
The worm secretes a hemolysin that lyses red cells inside the portal vessels
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large, non-operculated, yellowish-brown egg (140 x 60 µm) with a prominent, sharp lateral spine near the posterior pole, containing a fully developed ciliated miracidium.
questions.keyConcept: Schistosoma mansoni egg: Large lateral spine and ciliated miracidium.

questions.text: The structure indicated by the upper arrow is the:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Spindle-shaped egg (150 x 50 µm) with a straight, sharp terminal spine at the posterior pole.
questions.keyConcept: Schistosoma haematobium egg: Sharp terminal spine.

questions.text: This snail is the intermediate host of:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large ellipsoidal operculated egg (140 x 80 µm) filled with uniform granular yolk cells surrounding an unsegmented ovum.
questions.keyConcept: Fasciola hepatica egg: Operculated, unsegmented, large size.

questions.text: This patient was admitted with diarrhea and abdominal pain. His skin had a diffuse, rapidly moving, erythematous reticular rash from the anal margin to the upper legs. Which figure represents the stage found on stool examination?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Intestinal parasite causing diarrhea.
questions.keyConcept: Diagnostic stage in stool examination.

options: Balantidium coli cyst invading the mucosa
Cryptosporidium parvum stages on the brush border
Balantidium coli trophozoite at the brush border
Balantidium coli cyst at the brush border
Balantidium coli trophozoites invading the mucosa
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Minute, operculated, yellowish-brown egg (30 x 15 µm) with an indistinct opercular rim and a small knob-like thickening at the abopercular pole, containing a fully formed miracidium.
questions.keyConcept: Heterophyes heterophyes egg: Minute (30 µm), operculated with abopercular knob, mature miracidium.

questions.text: This snail is the first intermediate host of:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Spherical egg (35 µm) surrounded by a thick, brown, radially striated embryophore containing a 6-hooked hexacanth embryo (oncosphere).
questions.keyConcept: Taenia egg: Thick radially striated embryophore with 6-hooked oncosphere.

questions.text: Identify the station and the feature that identifies it:
options: Trichocephalus trichiurus in the appendix - bacillary band
Enterobius vermicularis in the appendix - double-bulbed esophagus seen in section
Enterobius vermicularis in the appendix - lateral cuticular alae
Ascaris lumbricoides in the appendix - thick cuticle
Strongyloides stercoralis in the mucosa - eggs in the uterus
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Spherical or subspherical translucent egg (45 µm) with two distinct membranes: outer thin membrane and inner embryophore displaying two polar knobs from which 4 to 8 polar filaments emerge into the space.
questions.keyConcept: Hymenolepis nana egg: Polar filaments emerging from polar knobs of embryophore.

questions.text: Growth retardation may be a manifestation of this parasitic infection. Interpret.
options: A bolus of adult worms causes intestinal obstruction
The adult worm absorbs most of the dietary vitamin B12
Autoinfective larvae destroy the intestinal villi
Egg granulomas cause periportal hepatic fibrosis
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large yellowish-brown egg (70 µm) with inner and outer membranes but completely LACKING polar filaments.
questions.keyConcept: Hymenolepis diminuta egg: Larger, no polar filaments.

questions.text: A patient has fever, tenesmus and dysentery. Sigmoidoscopy shows ulcers with a narrow opening, raised edge and wide base. Which figure represents the stage found in the ulcer biopsy?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Amebic dysentery with flask-shaped colonic ulcers. Diagnostic stage is Entamoeba histolytica with erythrophagocytosis.
questions.keyConcept: Entamoeba histolytica: Flask-shaped ulcers and bloody dysentery.

questions.text: Identify the station and the arrowed structure:
options: Taenia spp. mature segment - bilobed ovary
Taenia saginata gravid segment - central uterine stem
Taenia solium gravid segment - lateral uterine branches
Diphyllobothrium latum mature segment - rosette-shaped uterus
Diphyllobothrium latum mature segment - bilobed ovary
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Oval operculated egg (70 x 45 µm) with an inconspicuous opercular cap and a small abopercular knob, containing an unsegmented ovum.
questions.keyConcept: Diphyllobothrium latum egg: Operculated with abopercular knob, unsegmented.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Oval egg (60 x 40 µm) with blunt rounded poles, an extremely thin, transparent, clear shell, and an internal segmented ovum (morula stage with 4 to 8 blastomeres) separated from the shell by a clear space.
questions.keyConcept: Hookworm egg: Thin transparent shell with 4–8 blastomeres and clear space.

questions.text: Structure 2 in this egg is the:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Round/oval egg with a thick transparent inner shell covered by a golden-brown, coarsely tuberculated (mammillated) albuminous coat, containing a single unsegmented ovum.
questions.keyConcept: Fertilized Ascaris egg: Coarsely mammillated albuminous coat and unsegmented ovum.

questions.text: Layer 1 in this section is the:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Elongated, narrow, irregular egg (90 x 45 µm) with a thin shell and irregular mammillations filled with disorganized, highly refractile, atrophic yolk globules.
questions.keyConcept: Unfertilized Ascaris egg: Elongated, irregular mammillations, disorganized yolk granules.

questions.text: Identify the station and the type of anemia this parasite causes:
options: Anterior end of Strongyloides female - microcytic hypochromic anemia
Anterior end of Enterobius - normocytic normochromic anemia
Hookworm buccal capsule - microcytic hypochromic anemia
Hookworm buccal capsule - macrocytic megaloblastic anemia
Hookworm copulatory bursa - microcytic hypochromic anemia
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Fertilized Ascaris egg that has lost its outer mammillated albuminous coat, leaving a smooth, thick, transparent, colourless chitinous shell.
questions.keyConcept: Decorticated Ascaris egg: Smooth thick shell lacking outer mammillated layer.

questions.text: This parasitic stage is the pathogenic stage of:
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Asymmetric, plano-convex (D-shaped) egg with a double-contoured, transparent, smooth shell containing a fully formed, folded, coiled larva.
questions.keyConcept: Enterobius vermicularis egg: D-shaped (plano-convex) with coiled tadpole-like larva.

questions.text: A patient has pallor, puffy eyes and swollen feet. Which figure represents the stage that can be detected in his stool?
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Ancylostoma duodenale causes profound microcytic hypochromic iron deficiency anemia (0.2 mL blood loss/worm/day). Diagnostic stage is the thin-shelled 4-8 cell segmented egg.
questions.keyConcept: Hookworm anemia: Blood loss leads to pallor, puffy face, and edema; segmented morula egg.

questions.text: Identify the station and its relevance to man:
options: Cysticercus bovis - it causes human cysticercosis after eating the eggs
Hydatid cyst - man is an accidental intermediate host
Cysticercoid of H. nana - it develops in the human intestinal villi
Cysticercus cellulosae - it can develop in the human brain
Cysticercus bovis - man is infected by eating it in undercooked beef, but it does not develop in man
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Barrel-shaped (lemon-shaped / football-shaped) brown egg with two prominent, transparent, mucoid bipolar plugs, containing an unsegmented ovum.
questions.keyConcept: Trichuris trichiura egg: Barrel-shaped with prominent bipolar albuminous plugs.

questions.text: Identify the station and the arrowed structure:
options: Echinococcus granulosus scolex - rostellum with hooks
Taenia saginata scolex - rostellum with hooks
Taenia solium scolex - rostellum with hooks

questions.text: Finding this egg in a stool sample does NOT identify the species of the infecting worm. Interpret.
options: The egg is passed unembryonated, so the hexacanth embryo cannot be examined
The striated shell is dissolved by stool preservatives before examination
Eggs of T. saginata and T. solium are morphologically identical, so the gravid segment or scolex is needed
The egg is identical to the H. nana egg, which is the commonest cause
Eggs of T. solium are passed only in patients with cysticercosis
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Spherical acid-fast oocyst measuring 8–10 µm (twice the size of Cryptosporidium) showing variable acid-fast staining.
questions.keyConcept: Cyclospora oocyst: 8–10 µm spherical, variably acid-fast.

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Large ellipsoidal/spindle-shaped acid-fast oocyst (30 x 12 µm) with tapered ends containing 1 or 2 sporoblasts.
questions.keyConcept: Cystoisospora belli: Large spindle-shaped acid-fast oocyst (30 µm).

questions.text: Fatal hyperinfection with this parasite can occur in patients on corticosteroids. Interpret.
options: Eggs hatch in the stomach and release thousands of larvae
Larvae encyst in muscles and are released by steroids
Rhabditiform larvae turn into filariform larvae inside the gut and re-invade (autoinfection), so the worm load rises sharply when immunity falls
Adult worms multiply asexually in the liver
Steroids stimulate the female to lay unembryonated eggs
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Extremely tiny, oval, refractile microsporidial spores (1–2 µm) with a diagonal horizontal fluorescent/acid-fast polar belt.
questions.keyConcept: Microsporidia: Minute spores (1–2 µm).

questions.text: This parasite may cause megaloblastic anemia. Interpret.
options: The adult worm sucks blood from the intestinal mucosa
The adult worm in the small intestine takes up large amounts of dietary vitamin B12
The eggs embolize to the bone marrow
Larvae invade the stomach and destroy the parietal cells
questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Diphyllobothrium latum absorbs up to 80-100% of host dietary vitamin B12 in the ileum, producing megaloblastic / pernicious-like anemia.
questions.keyConcept: Diphyllobothrium latum megaloblastic anemia via vitamin B12 competition.

questions.text: Identify the arrowed stage. Why is it infective as soon as it is passed?

questions.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Cryptosporidium parvum oocysts sporulate inside the host enterocytes and are passed fully mature and immediately infective, containing 4 naked sporozoites.
questions.keyConcept: Cryptosporidium parvum: Passed fully sporulated with 4 sporozoites (immediate infectivity).

questions.text: A stool sample was received in your lab from a patient complaining of bloody diarrhea. Macroscopic appearance showed unformed stool with blood and mucus. Microscopic examination of the sample was done and revealed Gram-negative bacilli. What is the next step to identify the causative organism?
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: When a Gram-negative bacillus is visualized from a stool specimen causing bloody diarrhea (dysentery), the primary rapid biochemical step to differentiate Enterobacteriaceae (which are strictly oxidase-negative) from other Gram-negative enteric pathogens (such as Vibrio, Campylobacter, or Pseudomonas, which are oxidase-positive) is the oxidase test.

Option A, C, and D (indole, urease, citrate) are secondary biochemical reactions (part of the IMViC and differential panels) carried out only after confirming family placement and isolating pure colonies on differential/selective media.
questions.keyConcept: Oxidase test differentiates oxidase-negative Enterobacteriaceae (Shigella, Salmonella, E. coli) from oxidase-positive bacilli (Vibrio, Campylobacter, Pseudomonas).

media.caption: Gram stain of stool specimen showing Gram-negative bacilli

questions.text: After isolation of the previous stool sample, the following results were obtained: Oxidase negative, TSI showing alkaline slant / acid butt (K/A, red slant / yellow butt) with no gas and no H2S production, Citrate negative, and Motility negative. The causative agent is most likely:
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: Shigella species are non-motile, non-lactose fermenting Gram-negative bacilli that produce an alkaline slant / acid butt (K/A) on Triple Sugar Iron (TSI) agar without gas formation (glucose fermented without gas) and without H2S production. They are citrate-negative and oxidase-negative. Clinically, Shigella dysenteriae invades the colonic mucosa, producing acute bacillary dysentery characterized by painful cramps, tenesmus, and frequent stools containing blood, pus, and mucus.

Option A and B (ETEC, EHEC) are lactose fermenters (A/A on TSI with gas). Option C (Staph. aureus) is a Gram-positive coccus.
questions.keyConcept: Shigella dysenteriae: Non-motile, non-lactose fermenter, TSI K/A (no gas, no H2S), citrate-negative, causes bacillary dysentery.

media.caption: Biochemical reactions: Oxidase negative, TSI K/A (no gas, no H2S), Citrate negative

questions.text: To trace the source of the previous Shigella infection during an outbreak (epidemiological typing), which of the following can be used?
questions.explanation:
Criteria of Identification: Colicin typing (bacteriocin typing) is the established phenotypic method utilized for epidemiological source tracing and strain differentiation in outbreaks of Shigella sonnei and Shigella dysenteriae. Colicins are bacteriocins produced by certain bacterial strains that inhibit or kill closely related indicator strains.

Option B (Phage typing) is primarily used for Staphylococcus aureus and Salmonella typhi. Option C (Widal test) is an agglutination test for enteric fever (Salmonella). Option D (Serology) identifies O serogroups (A, B, C, D) but is insufficient alone for fine-scale epidemiological strain tracing.
questions.keyConcept: Colicin typing is the specific bacteriocin typing method used for epidemiological tracing of Shigella outbreaks.

questions.text: If isolation of the previous stool sample from a patient with bloody diarrhea had shown the following results instead: Oxidase negative, TSI showing acid slant / acid butt (A/A, yellow/yellow) with gas production, Indole positive (red ring), and Citrate negative, the causative agent would most likely be:
questions.explanation:
